title: Arcadia Amusements  -  1991 in review
_about: A showcase deck for the charts skill. Each slide's notes name the technique it demonstrates.

slides.title: Arcadia Amusements
slides.subtitle: 1991 in review  -  cabinets, coins and one very sad clam
slides.notes: TITLE SLIDE: a slide with no blocks. Title is drawn triple size, subtitle under a rule.

slides.title: December shipped three times as many cabinets as January
slides.subtitle: units per month, 1991

text: - June wobbled: see the next slide
> The white bar is December. One pinned colour does the pointing.

slides.notes: DASHBOARD: KPI strip (cols of stat) over a chart, commentary beside it, placed with at:[x,y,w,h] on the 12x12 grid. colors:{"Dec":"white"} paints ONE bar of a single-series chart. depth:3 makes the bars chunkier.

slides.title: Returns ran at a dozen a month...
slides.notes: BUILD, step 1: the plain chart, deliberately quiet (grey line, pinned axis) so the next slide can land. min/max are pinned so the two slides share an axis and nothing jumps.

slides.title: ...except June, when a bad batch of joysticks came back
slides.notes: BUILD, step 2: "like": 3 starts from slide 3's chart (every key but its place), and this slide adds only what is new: the annotations and the title that states the conclusion. All three annotation kinds: a callout (at), a level (y), a moment (x). Colour on an annotation carries meaning: red = the problem, green = the baseline.

slides.title: West grew from nothing special to half the business
slides.notes: COLOUR AS MEANING: grey out the context, give the one series you are talking about the bright colour. colors:{...} by series name. values:true on a stacked chart prints the totals.

slides.title: One game outsold the bottom four put together

annotations.text: 72. We do not talk about Sad Clam.

slides.notes: RANKING + SHARE: hbar for long names (sort the CSV descending first), a pie3d with explode:0 popping the winner out. rows/cols nest: the right column is a rows group holding a chart and bullets. legend:false when the neighbour already names everything.

slides.title: Coin boxes fill up, then the machine starts to fail
slides.notes: SCATTER: the CSV says '#chart: xy' so its first numeric column is X. A note:[x,y] annotation is free text anywhere in the plot: use it for sample size, source, caveats.

slides.title: Most plays last under five minutes

text: > A histogram wants one numeric column and nothing else.
blocks.title: reading this

slides.notes: HISTOGRAM + BOXED TEXT: hist takes the first series; bins sets the buckets. box:true puts text in a framed window with its own title, so it sits as an equal beside the chart. palette can change per chart.

slides.title: Same quarter, four regions: small multiples share an axis
slides.notes: SMALL MULTIPLES: layout:grid, one series per panel via series_col, and the SAME min/max on every panel so heights compare across panels. One panel in a different colour is the one to look at.

slides.title: Uptime never fell below 97%, even in June
slides.subtitle: cabinets working, % of opening hours
slides.notes: BROKEN AXIS: min 95 zooms in on the part that matters, and because bars are read by their length charts tears them just off the baseline and puts a double slash through the axis, so nobody reads June as a third of January. Use it for bars only when the differences are the story; a line chart needs no break.

slides.title: Laser Llama earns the most, and the same everywhere
slides.subtitle: coins per cabinet per day, mean over 15 sites; whiskers from the worst site to the best

annotations.text: 95 to 300: it depends where it stands

slides.notes: ERROR BARS: errors names other columns of the same file and they become whiskers instead of bars: [low, high] columns here, or one column for +-. Show the spread whenever the data has one; a difference inside the whiskers is not a finding.

slides.title: Doubling the price lifted every title but the clam
slides.subtitle: dollars per cabinet per day, before and after the 50c price
slides.notes: DUMBBELL: before and after per category, a series for each state. The arrow points at the last series, so direction reads before the numbers do. Grey out 'before' and colour 'after': the eye goes to where things ended up.

slides.title: A returned cabinet is back on the floor in nine days
slides.notes: FLOW: name the steps and the arrows; charts lays them out in columns, bends the arrows, and runs the loop back (QA -> repair) as a straight line. Colour only the steps that mean something: green is where you want to end up, red is the loss. Label the arrows with what moves or when.

slides.title: The hits stand by the door; the clam is in the back
slides.notes: SHAPES: free drawing on a 12 x 12 grid over the block. Rectangles, ellipses, polygons, arrows and labels; a colour makes a shape solid, depth extrudes it like a bar, dither mixes in the background, shadow drops a DOS shadow. Draw only what makes the point: here, where things stand.

slides.title: The receipts
slides.notes: TABLES: when someone will ask for the exact number. Columns of words come along, and numbers keep the decimals the CSV wrote (2995.00 stays 2,995.00). Put them near the end.

slides.title: One palette per mood
slides.notes: PALETTES: dos ega cga ice fire green amber mono. Set one on the deck for a consistent look, override per chart for contrast. mono uses dither patterns instead of colour.

text: - Twelve-hour duty cycle, then a rest
slides.notes: CLOSING: a one-block text slide. size:2 doubles the text; keep it to a handful of short lines. valign:middle centres it vertically.
